Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexGen SecureTech Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexGen SecureTech's results for the second quarter fiscal year 2024. With me on today's call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Security Officer; and Jordan Lee, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. NexGen SecureTech continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the second quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about Nexus AI platform and the resulting 50% reduction in mean time to detect advanced threats is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: providing commentary on the evolving threat landscape, driving expansion within existing large accounts, acquiring new customers at scale, making progress on key strategic initiatives, accelerating ARR growth rates both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, and improving competitive win rates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Before diving into our Q2 results, I want to spend a few minutes providing some color on the evolving threat landscape, as it's not only shaping our day-to-day operations but also driving the secular tailwinds behind our 28% year-over-year revenue growth and expanding margins. As you know, the cybersecurity market is projected to exceed $250 billion globally by 2026, per Gartner, fueled by an unrelenting surge in sophisticated attacks. Let me break this down with the latest data and trends we're seeing across our platform, which protected over 15,000 enterprise customers last quarter.

First, ransomware remains the apex predator, accounting for 42% of all incidents we mitigated in Q2—up from 31% a year ago. According to our telemetry, the average ransomware payload size has ballooned 65% year-over-year to over 1.2 terabytes, with double-extortion tactics now standard in 78% of cases. We're seeing attackers like LockBit 3.0 and BlackCat evolve their encryptors to evade EDR solutions, incorporating polymorphic code that mutates in real-time. A prime example was the Q2 breach at a major U.S. healthcare provider—similar to the Change Healthcare incident earlier this year—where attackers exfiltrated 4TB of protected health information before encryption, demanding $22 million. Our endpoint platform blocked 2.3 million such attempts across our customer base, a 150% increase from Q2 2023.

Shifting to AI-driven threats, which now represent 22% of our high-severity alerts, we're witnessing a proliferation of generative AI weapons. Phishing kits leveraging tools like WormGPT have driven a 240% year-over-year spike in credential-stuffing attacks, with success rates climbing to 18% thanks to hyper-personalized lures via deepfake voice synthesis. We've observed over 500,000 AI-generated phishing emails per day in Q2, mimicking executive signatures with 95% accuracy. This isn't hypothetical—recall the MGM Resorts attack in 2023, where social engineering bypassed MFA; we're now seeing vishing campaigns targeting SOC analysts directly.

Supply chain compromises are another red-hot vector, up 112% year-over-year per our data. Post-Log4Shell and MOVEit, attackers are chaining vulnerabilities like the recent Ivanti EPMM zero-day CVE-2024-29824, which we patched proactively for 40% of our customers. Nation-state actors, particularly from APT41 out of China and Sandworm from Russia, are embedding backdoors in open-source packages—our NPM scanner flagged 1,200 malicious modules last quarter alone.

On the cloud front, misconfigurations continue to plague hybrid environments. With 68% of breaches originating in multi-cloud setups—AWS S3 buckets being the weakest link in 55% of cases—we've seen identity-based attacks explode 190% year-over-year. Think Okta's 2022 breach or the Snowflake incidents this summer, where stolen session tokens granted persistent access. Our SSE platform enforced zero-trust segmentation for 85% of our cloud workloads, reducing mean time to detect from the 21-day industry average to under 4 hours.

Regionally, the landscape is fracturing. In North America, which drove 52% of our bookings, ransomware targets critical infrastructure—healthcare saw a 180% attack surge amid HIPAA pressures. EMEA, at 28% of revenue, faces state-sponsored espionage; we've blocked 15,000+ Cobalt Group campaigns since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, with ICS/OT exploits up 95%. APAC is the growth hotspot at 20% year-over-year, but mobile threats via Android malware like FluBot have tripled, hitting financial services hard in India and Southeast Asia where 5G adoption is at 45%.

Strategically, this chaos is our opportunity. We're leaning into XDR convergence—our integrated platform now fuses EDR, NDR, and CNAPP with AI-driven behavioral analytics, achieving 99.2% true positive rates and slashing false positives by 70%. We've invested $250 million in R&D this year for quantum-resistant algorithms like Kyber and Dilithium, ahead of NIST's post-quantum standards, and partnered with Microsoft to embed our tech into Azure Sentinel. Early adopters of our Zero Trust Exchange saw a 40% drop in lateral movement risks.

Looking forward, we expect threat volumes to rise another 35% in FY24, per our forward-looking models, but dwell time is plummeting—down to 11 days globally thanks to ML anomaly detection. This dynamic validates our land-and-expand model: 65% of Q2 ACV expansion came from threat-informed upsells like deception tech and autonomous SOAR.

We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the second quarter was $285 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 92% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 82%, while operating expenses were $210 million. Net income was $52 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.72. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

I'm thrilled to dive into one of our strongest growth drivers this quarter: expansion within our existing large accounts. Our land-and-expand model has been a cornerstone of NexGen SecureTech's success in the cybersecurity landscape, where we power over 2,500 enterprise customers with our integrated platform encompassing EDR, XDR, SASE, and our AI-native CWPP.

In Q2 FY24, expansion revenue from existing large accounts—defined as those with over $1 million in ARR—reached $178 million, representing a robust 42% year-over-year increase and accounting for 68% of our total new ARR bookings. This drove our dollar-based net retention rate to an industry-leading 128% for the quarter, up from 122% a year ago. To put that in perspective, the average cybersecurity peer hovers around 115-120% NRR. Our outperformance underscores the stickiness of our modular architecture, where customers seamlessly layer on capabilities without rip-and-replace disruptions.

Breaking it down by cohort, our top 100 large accounts—primarily Fortune 500 financial institutions, healthcare providers, and critical infrastructure operators—expanded at an even faster clip, with average ACV growth of 32% per account. For instance, we saw 145 accounts upsell into our full XDR suite, adding an average of $450K in incremental ARR each, fueled by the integration of our GenAI-powered threat hunting module. Customers like a major U.S. bank reduced MTTD for advanced persistent threats by 65% post-deployment, prompting them to consolidate their legacy SIEM and expand across 75,000 endpoints.

Regionally, in the Americas, which comprise 62% of our large account base, expansions grew 48% year-over-year to $110 million, propelled by U.S. SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules and CMMC 2.0 compliance. We've landed expansions in 12 of the top 20 U.S. banks, bundling our SASE with ZTNA.

EMEA delivered 35% year-over-year growth to $42 million, with traction in DACH and the Nordics under NIS2. A pan-European energy giant expanded from EDR to our full-stack SASE, citing our 99.999% uptime.

APAC, at 55% year-over-year to $26 million, benefited from supply chain fears echoing MOVEit, with 28 Japanese financial services firms integrating our CWPP.

These expansions reflect our platformization push: 82% involved cross-selling across product families via our Nexus dashboard. Customer success-led motions included 17 zero-day mitigations, and AI investments like our Autonomous Response Engine sped expansions 2.5x. Our pipeline stands at $1.2 billion, up 30% quarter-over-quarter.

Good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO, I'm thrilled to dive into our ARR performance, the cornerstone of our subscription-driven model. For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, we delivered total ARR of $528 million, marking a robust 15.2% quarter-over-quarter growth from $458 million in Q1, and an exceptional 48.7% year-over-year increase from $355 million in Q2 FY2023. This acceleration outpaces the broader market's estimated 14% CAGR through 2028, per Gartner.

QoQ, our 15.2% sequential growth came from new logos and expansions, with NRR at 128%. Expansions were 62% of new ARR, including 147 net new customers and 12 enterprises over $1 million ARR in financials and healthcare.

YoY, the 48.7% reflects strategic investments, with average ARR per customer up 22% to $1.47 million, driven by our CNWP module at 82% YoY.

North America contributed 68% of ARR with 52% YoY growth on CISA mandates. EMEA surged 67% on NIS2, APAC 71% via Tencent Cloud.

We've seen a 35% QoQ uptick in ARR from GenAI Threat Intelligence, countering 41% ransomware rise. Churn sub-3%, RPO $2.5 billion up 55% YoY. We guide Q3 ARR to 16-18% QoQ and 50%+ YoY.

I'll now dive into our customer momentum. In Q2, we acquired 452 new customers, marking a 28% quarter-over-quarter increase from 353 in Q1, and 42% year-over-year from 318 in Q2 2023. This exceeded our guidance of 400-425, amid ransomware like LockBit 3.0 and Ivanti zero-days.

In enterprise ($1M+ ARR), 128 new logos, up 35% QoQ and 55% YoY, including three Fortune 100 financials migrating to Nexus XDR and a top-5 cloud provider's ZTNA, averaging $2.8M ACV.

Mid-market (250K-$1M), 195 customers, 26% QoQ via Nexus SASE and Guardian AI, with MSSPs like Optiv.

SMB under 250K, 129, 22% QoQ through 1,200 VARs on AWS/Azure Marketplace.

North America 62% (280), EMEA 22% (100) on NIS2, APAC 12% (54) on APTs, LATAM 4% (18).

Our platform consolidation, AI innovation, and vertical focus like OT/IoT drove this. Q3 guide 475-525 adds.

Before I hand over, our competitive win rates: in Q2, 68%, up 6 points YoY from 62%, driving $150M ARR from displacements, 42% of new ACV.

EDR/XDR: 72%, 78% over CrowdStrike/Microsoft via QuantumShield's 45% false positive cut, 100% MITRE coverage.

CNAPP/SSE: 75%, 82% over Palo Alto/Zscaler, $25M hyperscaler win.

SASE/ZTNA: 64%, edging Netskope/Cisco.

North America 70%, EMEA 66%, APAC 65%. Driven by R&D, SecureNet Challenge pilots at 85% conversion, partners like Snowflake. Expect 70-72% FY24.

With that, I'll pass to Dr. Novak.

Dr. Lena Novak: Thank you, Mike. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include advancing our Nexus AI for hypergraph anomaly detection, expanding zero-trust coverage to 92% of MITRE ATT&CK, scaling CloudShield XDR with 15.5 petabytes telemetry, and pioneering post-quantum cryptography with QuantumShield.

Raj Patel: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with proactive patches, zero-day mitigations, and zero-trust enforcement reducing risks across endpoints, cloud, and networks.

Jordan Lee: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well, and we are expanding our channel partnerships to reach a wider audience, with 55% of SMB wins via MSSPs and marketplaces, and healthy pipelines in EMEA and APAC.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: please press star then one if you have a question. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mike, can you expand on the ARR acceleration and how expansions contributed to the 15.2% QoQ growth?

Sarah Chen: Thanks, John. As Mike detailed, the 15.2% QoQ ARR jump to $528 million was propelled by expansions making up 62% of new bookings, with NRR at 128%. Our land-and-expand is working, especially in large accounts upsell to XDR and Zero Trust Edge, alongside new logos. This positions us strongly against peers.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Great results. Mike, on the competitive win rates improving to 68%, what specific factors drove the gains in EDR/XDR and cloud-native, and any pipeline color?

Mike Thompson: Emily, thanks. The 68% win rate, up from 62% YoY, stemmed from technical edges like 45% fewer false positives in QuantumShield XDR, 100% MITRE detection, and agentless CNAPP beating Prisma Cloud in 82% of multi-cloud evals. Pipeline $1.2 billion with 55% competitive, expecting 70-72% FY24 as we roll out ML risk policies.

Operator: Next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel: Impressive new customer adds. Dr. Novak, how is the Nexus AI platform contributing to these wins, particularly in mid-market and APAC?

Dr. Lena Novak: David, Nexus AI has been pivotal, with 145% YoY detections blocking 2.7 billion threats and MTTD under 3 minutes. In mid-market, Guardian AI cut false positives 65% in betas, converting 72% of POCs. APAC growth 89% via telco embeds countering APT41, fueling 54 new logos there.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong: On the threat landscape, Raj, how are nation-state actors like APT41 and Sandworm impacting your CSO priorities, and mitigations?

Raj Patel: Lisa, those actors are embedding backdoors in packages—we flagged 1,200 malicious NPM modules—and chaining vulns like Ivanti. Priorities include XDR fusion at 99.2% true positives, proactive patching for 40% customers, and quantum-resistant algos, dropping dwell time to 11 days while blocking Cobalt Group campaigns.

Sarah Chen: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
